"If you have institutions, culture, and education — you will not be poor." – Secretary of Energy @SecretaryWright shared a powerful and personal message at the Cato Institute event.

Watch the full conversation: piped.video/KGmzgrYNSKk

Join @thomaschattwill for a discussion with Cato research fellow @Rhetors_of_York about the existential crisis facing American liberalism, and how we might move beyond the current impasse toward a more integrated and resilient public square. nitter.net/i/broadcasts/1NGaraYQn…

Government made it too hard to build homes — and tariffs made it more expensive. 

That’s why housing is so expensive. The fix: legalize more housing, speed up permits, open up land, and end trade barriers. Cato's @sslivinski explains.

Video

Energy affordability starts with getting government out of the way. 

Cutting red tape and liberalizing federal permitting lets markets deliver cheaper, more abundant energy for American families. 

Check out the Cato Institute Handbook on Affordability to learn more:
ow.ly/ulE350YYnsB

"Capitalists” aren't conspiring against workers — and the zero-sum narrative is wrong. But people still worried about a declining “labor share” should stop blaming corporations and start fixing all the government policies that discourage hiring, trap workers in jobs, and block mobility, explains Cato's @scottlincicome. 

ow.ly/2vCA50Z0bio

Join us for a conversation with @JohnHCochrane, @DavidRMalpass, and @ocampo_emilio discussing the benefits of dollarization to Latin American countries with a history of bad monetary policy, why dollarization in the Americas would be good for the United States, and how adopting the dollar as the legal currency has worked out in Panama, Ecuador, and El Salvador. The speakers will discuss ways of dollarizing and why that reform is especially relevant to Argentina and Venezuela today.
nitter.net/i/

Consumer goods are less affordable today than a year ago—the first time this has happened in three years. But there are solutions. 

Cato scholars have developed 100+ policy ideas to defuse inflation and lower the cost of living: cato.org/handbook-affordabil…

Over 70 educational freedom programs now operate across more than 30 states — a remarkable expansion of school choice in America. 

Cato's @ColleenHroncich identifies the five key components every successful program needs and shows how states like Florida and Arizona are leading the way.

ow.ly/fSuA50YXRfv

President Trump is right to withdraw troops from Germany and from Europe, explain Cato’s @JustinTLogan and American Ideas Institute’s Sumantra Maitra:

“German and broader European security do not require American power in theater by the division.”

ow.ly/KjGO50YZyQX

Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 sat dormant for 50 years for good reason. In a new Cato Podcast episode, @clark_packard and @AlfredCObregon break down why courts keep rejecting the administration’s tariff theories and what the looming Section 301 investigations mean for American importers.

Listen on Apple, Spotify, and our website!

Apple: ow.ly/7KnG50YZAA1 
Spotify: ow.ly/4HRf50YZAA0 
Website: ow.ly/sfHy50YZAzV

Join us for a conversation with President and CEO of DonorsTrust @Lawson_Bader, Cato Senior Fellow @walterolson, and President of the John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation @jpalfrey on the importance of philanthropic freedom and what’s at stake when the state asserts authority over private giving.
nitter.net/i/broadcasts/1yxBeMozB…

We were honored to host Secretary of Energy @SecretaryWright at the Cato Institute for a wide-ranging conversation on the current state of energy policy — and the market revolutions to come. 

Watch the full discussion on YouTube and our website.

YouTube: ow.ly/uk8S50YZMJn 
Website: ow.ly/w43m50YZMJ6

Drug prohibition was never the solution — it was the problem. Cato's @dr4liberty explains why protecting people means trusting them to make their own choices.

Video

High gas prices stem from the Iran War, not the gas tax. But the gas tax should still be repealed to let states fund the 98% of roads they already own, says Cato's @adamnmichel.

Key homebuilding inputs are made more expensive both by existing and newly imposed import tariffs. 

To improve housing affordability, tariffs on home construction materials and appliances should be eliminated, says Cato’s @sslivinski. 

Learn more in the Cato “Handbook on Affordability”: ow.ly/tN8y50YYoei
